title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero's Monster Cooking
text: “Big bro! Over here, over here!”

My little brother was waving at us from the train platform. He was holding a huge suitcase in one hand and carrying a backpack so big on his back that he looked like a backpacker. What on earth is this guy bringing with him…?
“Yeah, yeah. For someone carrying such a huge load, you sure are heading out early.”
“Yeah, he sure was excited while getting ready.”

As for why I’m about to get on the train with my little brother… it’s because we’re going on a trip to visit relatives in the countryside. Of course, Raphtalia is coming along too. Our parents still have work to do, so they’re planning to join us at our relatives’ place later. Atla? She’ll catch up with us later, right? Well, she might be causing a ruckus right now in front of our house. She did sneak out without asking. A loud noise echoes as the train signals its departure, so we hurry aboard and head to the seats indicated on our tickets to take our seats. The front car was my little brother’s choice. He picked it because he wanted to see the scenery, or something like that. That’s the kind of train trip this is.
“Off to the countryside with you, big bro! I’m so excited!”
“Weren’t you planning on playing galge games at home?”
“That wouldn’t have been so bad, though. I just felt like it.”
So capricious.
“The whole point of this trip to the countryside is probably to get you to help out with all sorts of things, so I’m just going to take it easy.”
“No, this is a trip for everyone, right?”
Why is it a given that I’m the one who’s supposed to help out? Our parents will probably join us later and we’ll go see the local tourist spots and stuff.

“I wonder. Oh, Raphtalia, you’ve got to make sure you stay right by my brother’s side—otherwise, those country folk might try to pull some trouble just to get free labor, so you’ve got to be careful.”
“Oh, okay.”
“So why are you being so weirdly on guard…?”
It’s just the countryside.
“Well, I hope it turns out to be a fun trip—I’d love to try some game dishes made from what that hunter uncle catches.”
“Yeah, me too.”
Though I’ll probably end up having to help out quite a bit.
“Maybe this time you’ll let my brother use a hunting rifle?”
“I think he said it was an air rifle, not a hunting rifle… He seems to treasure it, so I doubt he’ll let me shoot it.”
You can actually hunt wild animals with an air rifle, right?
“Air rifles and air guns are different, you know? Hehe… Naofumi-san, you have your cute moments. You use such funny turns of phrase.”
…I kind of feel like Itsuki is making fun of me in my head, but is that just my imagination?
“Guns, huh?”
“I guess guns aren’t used much in your country, Raphtalia-san?”
“Yes, that’s… right.”
Well, there really wasn’t much need for guns in that other world. I guess the only one who could really handle them was Itsuki, the Bow Hero.
“In my case, when it comes to monsters… no, animals, I’d probably cut them down or beat them to death.”
“Haha, you’re pretty good at jokes too, Raphtalia.”

Hmm… Raphtalia still hasn’t fully caught up with Japanese social norms yet. Just as we were sitting in our train seats chatting casually… the moment the train entered the tunnel, a strange sensation occurred in my field of vision—something like a double image, or perhaps the outlines of red and blue blurring—and the train began to shake violently. I could sense it instinctively, a chill running down my spine.
“W-what is it?”
My younger brother reacted too.
“This is—”
“Ugh…”
We tried to figure out what was happening and deal with it, but nothing we did worked, and we—

Just as the double, blurring vision suddenly cleared, the lights flickered, and the moment we emerged from the tunnel… the train came to a screeching halt. Looking out the window—or rather, at the front of the train—there were no tracks ahead. Looking back through the window, even the tunnel we’d just passed through… wasn’t there either. So… the view outside the window is pretty nice—or rather, it’s a grassy plain. There’s no way you’d see a grassy plain with a horizon like this right after passing through a mountain tunnel near a residential area. Well, it’s just a gut feeling, but it feels like we’ve ended up somewhere other than Japan. It’s like… I can sense the atmosphere of another world based on experience.
“Naofumi, Sa…n. What’s going on?”

As always, it still bugs me that Raphtalia calls me “-san” so casually. It’s as if the way people address me—including the honorific “-sama”—has become established; I guess they’ve been using it as part of my name all along. …But honestly, being addressed with “-sama” makes people around me look at me more critically, so I really wish she’d get used to it.
“Ah… probably.”

Since Raphtalia asked me in a low voice, I agreed and placed my hand on the accessory shield, trying to tap into the power of the spirits and the God Hunters. …The response is weak. There’s no sign that I’ll be able to make contact. It’s a really bad feeling.
“Huh? When did the train stop!?”
“What’s going on!?”
The passengers sitting in their seats look out the window and, with cries of surprise, begin to panic.
“E-everyone, please stay calm!”
The conductor, who had been driving, steps out of the driver’s cab and shouts. He’s definitely the most flustered of them all.
“He looks the most flustered, doesn’t he? That conductor.”
My younger brother lets out a wry “Haha.” You sure have a laid-back reaction, don’t you?
“Hey! What the hell is going on here!?”
Some middle-aged guy is bearing down on the conductor with such force it looks like he’s about to pounce.
“My phone’s out of range—I can’t get a signal!”
“No signal at all!”
“I mean, where the hell are we anyway!?”
“All of a sudden, we’re in a grassland…”
“Hey. Over there… I see some buildings.”

As I turned my head toward where the passenger sitting on my side was pointing… sure enough, there were buildings. I could see stone structures scattered about—they didn’t look like traditional Japanese houses. It felt like a village. From that direction, a group of people who didn’t look Japanese—carrying tools like hoes—were approaching us warily.
“W-what should we do…”
“Hey, isn’t this one of those ‘reincarnation in another world’ things I’ve seen in online novels?”
“You idiot, I didn’t die—this is a transfer.”
“Huh? Aren’t they the same thing?”
“Nope. If you’re reincarnating, you’ve gotta die.”
“Huh!? Are you making fun of me?”
“It’s called a ‘summoning,’ right?”
“Who summoned me, then? There’s no spellcaster here.”
Ah, there are people on this train who have a vague understanding of the concept and can’t even tell the difference between reincarnation, transfer, and summoning.
“This is such a dream-like situation! Big bro! It’s exciting, isn’t it? You used to love stuff like this, right?”

……My little brother thinks he understands me and is making fun of me. Well, sure, the idea of a dream-like summoning or transfer to another world would’ve gotten me excited back in the day, but I’ve had more than enough of that now. I’ve finally made it back to Japan after overcoming a battle that ended up saving not just one world, but countless worlds. But even if I explained it, he probably wouldn’t believe me.
“I like it, but it’d be a pain if it actually happened, right?”
I’ll just give him that safe answer.
“Yeah… I’d rather not deal with that.”
As for Raphtalia, her response makes it clear she just wants a peaceful life in Japan.
“Still, Naofumi… if you say it’s okay, I’ll do my best.”
“It doesn’t have to go that far.”

I’d like to go home as soon as possible. I’d prefer to wrap this up by having it turn out to be a dream and get back on track with my original trip. But my shield and those kinds of powers don’t seem to be working properly. It looks like I can transform it into a shield, though.
“Really? The old you would’ve been excited about this—I think you’d happily choose to stay permanently, and I’m sure you could live anywhere.”
“You’re not wrong.”
So even Raphtalia isn’t on my side about this… Honestly, I can’t deny it.
“I get the feeling you’ve made your peace with becoming independent from Mom and Dad, right?”
“Don’t go thinking you understand me all that well.”
It’s not wrong, though. I just want to go home.
“Wait… could it be that you guys are from another world?”
A group of people who look like foreigners are addressing us as we sit on the train, observing the situation. Raphtalia tried to step forward, but—
“Hey, conductor! You’re in charge here, right?”
“Y-yes.”
So, I went over to talk to the group who’d called out to us—essentially after being shooed off the train by the other passengers.
“W-well, my name is…”
“Huh?”

It seemed like they understood what I was saying. Based on their appearance alone, they looked like they might speak English… though their pronunciation was a bit off as they tried to carry on a conversation.
“Oh, you understand me. Um…”
“Let me ask again. Did you guys come from another world?”
“Another world…”
“Yeah, you came out of what looked like a metal box—something we don’t see in this world—so I figured that might be the case.”
“Eh…”
Ugh, the conductor’s reaction is slow. He’s the type of ordinary person who just doesn’t get that sort of thing. The kind of guy who only studied and never really enjoyed stories like this.
“Ugh, this is such a hassle! I’ll handle it!”
So, one of the passengers who seemed to grasp the situation best got off the train to talk to the locals.
“Bro, should I go?”
“If you want to go, why not?”
My little brother’s actually pretty good with people.
“I’ll be right back!”
My little brother quickly slipped into the group. I guess you could say he’s energetic. If this were me back in the day, I probably would’ve reacted the same way.

“Hello, hello. I was the one piloting that vehicle over there. I don’t know how advanced your civilization is, but if we treat you like some kind of horse rider, we won’t get anywhere, so he and I are going to ask you about the situation.”

Saying that, my younger brother starts talking. Well… I guess I’ll just have to stay quiet, check out the surroundings, and try to communicate using my God-Hunting power. Around here… I get the feeling there’s a monster-like presence, though it doesn’t seem to be too close.
“So, you mentioned another world—given the situation, I suppose that’s probably the case, right? So, what exactly do you want to tell us?”
“Ah… I heard that phenomena like this happen about once every few decades.”
“I see…”
“This village isn’t exactly wealthy, but apparently it wouldn’t be right to just expel people from another world, so we have to report this to the lord and, just in case, notify the kingdom as well.”
This is such a classic dialogue flow… In my case, I was summoned to the castle as a hero. Then, Raphtalia stands next to me and whispers,
“So you’ve been transported to another world?”
“I don’t think that’s something that happens all the time…”
“I wonder. We’ll have to figure out the cause.”
“Yeah.”
I should probably start thinking about getting back to Japan as soon as possible.
“Anyway, it’d be a problem if we got attacked by monsters while talking here. It’d be a big help if you could come with us to the village—what do you say?”
“What if I say no?”
“I’ll file a report, so do whatever you want. Just know that if a crime is committed, we’ll take appropriate action.”
It seems my younger brother and the villagers had coordinated their information, so I ended up being escorted to the village.
“No! I’m staying right here! You guys should leave already!”

There’s someone making a hysterical scene over there. She’s either completely clueless about the situation, or she’s probably hoping that if she’s on a train, she’ll be able to return to her original world.
“Hey. It doesn’t look like anything’s going to change if you stay here.”
“That’s not necessarily true! I can go back!”
She’s making a real racket. Escaping reality… I get why she’d want to, but if it were that easy to go back, I’d be staying here too.
“Sigh…”
Then, my younger brother let out a huge sigh and broke into what looked like a professional smile.
“If you want to stay, that’s fine with me. We’re splitting up anyway—we’re basically castaways ourselves, so we’re not really your companions. Go ahead, go ahead.”
“What’s that supposed to mean! Don’t just go ahead and decide things on your own!”

“I’m just not going with you, okay? You can do whatever you want, and I’m suggesting that whoever wants to come along should come along. I’m going to follow their guide. That’s all I’ve decided—it’s not like I need your permission, is it?”
“Huh? I don’t get it. Isn’t this the kind of thing where we take a majority vote?”
“Look… what’s the point of deciding by majority vote? I’m the one who doesn’t get it here. Seriously.”

I can’t keep up with this. “So, what’s everyone going to do?” My brother seems to be subtly stirring things up… Well, I guess I have to go along with this much. I’d do the same if I were in his shoes. My brother usually cares a lot about appearances, but this is the kind of situation we’re in.
“How should I put it… that kind of detachment—you can tell he’s Lord Naofumi’s brother, right?”
Raphtalia seems to understand something, too.
“Is that what I’m like?”
“It’s a reaction similar to what Lord Naofumi described when dealing with strange people—as the Spear Hero once said. The words and attitude may be different, but it hasn’t changed even now.”
“Is that so…?”
I wonder if that’s really what I’m like from an objective perspective.
“Hey! What’s with that attitude?! Are you trying to cause trouble for the rescue team by acting on your own?!”
Now some middle-aged guy is making a fuss.
“Then why don’t you just stay here? I’m going to gather intel. That’s all. Can you cut it out already?”
Cutting him off sharply, the younger brother came back over to us.
“What are you going to do, big bro? You’re coming, right?”
“Well, yeah.”
The younger brother had been glancing my way several times, and I’d been signaling back that I’d probably head toward the village too.
“It’s a bit far from the village, so I wouldn’t recommend staying here forever.”
“There are bandits around, so be careful, okay?”
The villagers’ attitude was more like, “If you want to stay here, we can’t help it”—almost like a threat.
“What’s that supposed to mean! Cut it out already!”

And then, the hysterical woman started screaming. She’s glaring at my younger brother. Oh well. I guess I’ll have to put on a little act. I think this is a bit much, and if I don’t say something back… my brother might end up on her bad side.

“We’re not your guardians. We’re not affiliated with the train company either—we’re just fellow passengers caught up in the accident. Stop making a scene and trying to manipulate everyone around you.”
“Whoa, big brother sure has a mouth on him.”
“Well, I was a little concerned about that lady, too.”
“Haaaaaaaaaa!? That’s impossible! I’m definitely going to expose you guys!”
“Where are you going to expose us? Your phone doesn’t even have service.”
I wasn’t about to put up with this. It’s best to stay away from people like that, so I grabbed our stuff and headed out.
“Hey—! Don’t take my stuff!”
“This is our stuff.”
“Oh, so you were after someone else’s stuff? You’re quite the monster. Worse than a demon. Haha.”
I pointed right at her.
“What did you just sayyyyyyyy!?”
Man, she’s really screaming her head off. Bitch was even more of a pain. Well, I guess she’s in a different league compared to that guy. …Though it’s a league I’d rather not be in.
“Haha! This is hilarious.”
My little brother’s following suit too… but you’ve got way too much stuff. What’s even in there?
“Ugh, seriously… these brothers… Naofumi, it seems like there’s been an increase in the ‘n’s.”

Raphtalia is sighing. I know I’m being mean, but I can’t stick around with a guy like that. The passengers, including the conductor, seemed to be whispering among themselves, deciding whether to stay or go to the village. In the end, fewer chose to stay, so we headed to the village… where we were assigned temporary lodging—a fairly exposed open square and an unused shed—and settled in to rest. As for food… we were given dried meat, bread, and water. It seemed like we could drink as much water as we wanted if we just drew it from the well.
So… while we were being shown to our resting places in the village, the sun began to set.
“Um. What about dinner…?”
“Please make do with what we’ve given you.”

Word had gotten around the village—or rather, to the relevant people—and we ended up waiting for someone to come and take care of us, but since we weren’t exactly being welcomed, the meal turned out to be very simple. As for the meal, Raphtalia just had a light snack of dried meat and bread and didn’t seem to have any complaints. She’s used to this, isn’t she? Just as I thought.
“Just getting a meal is enough, right? After all, this isn’t something they can just hand out easily.”
“That’s true.”
I guess the villagers were sharing what little food they had with us.
“There’s not nearly enough to fill us up, though. But we should be grateful for what we get, right?”

To begin with, some of the passengers were actually carrying food—or rather, luggage—with them. Those hysterical women were probably trying to get us to divide up the edible food we had fairly among everyone.
“Sigh… Even in another world, having only dried meat and bread for a meal…”
One of our fellow passengers who’d come over to the village is grumbling.
“Go tell them that.”
“The villagers should give us something better to eat.”
“I wish they’d set up a soup kitchen or something—at least some soup would be nice.”
Everyone was having a simple meal. Just then, one of the passengers—some kind of high-and-mighty college student about my age—stood up straight, puffed out his chest, and took a step forward.
“I’m gonna cook something delicious for everyone! I’m gonna blow the locals away with my cooking! Hehehe… I’m gonna make it big as a chef in this other world!”
He was bragging like that. It’s typical for the capable ones to step up at times like this. “I’m going to blow the locals away with modern cuisine!” That’s the classic approach.
“Still, how are you even going to cook?”
“Haha! I majored in culinary arts, and I just happened to have all kinds of stuff in my luggage.”
He’s pretty lucky. He pulls out cooking utensils—a pot and a frying pan—and flashes a pocket knife. I guess his timing is just right. He seems to have all sorts of other basic tools, too.
“Whoa…”
“This is a lifesaver!”
“Hahaha, just watch me!”
With that, he started a fire and began preparing.
“I’m going to eat what my big brother makes, so I don’t need any! It’ll be way tastier!”
My little brother is trying to one-up me for some reason.
“Well… that’s true, I guess. But I don’t see the point in competing.”
I agree with Raphtalia. Why? Do I have to be the one to cook?
“If someone else is going to make it, isn’t that fine?”
“No way, no way! I want to eat what my big brother cooks!”
And so, my younger brother threw a tantrum.
“Even so, it’s not something you can just whip up easily, is it?”

Could I use the stuff in my shield or something? Well, I could probably use a rock lying around to make a makeshift griddle or bowl. Worst case, even a notebook would do—as long as I have paper and water, I could probably make some soup with hot water.
“Hehe! Don’t underestimate me.”

And with that, my little brother opened his unnecessarily huge suitcase… and out came all the kitchen utensils we had at home, along with a cooler. You didn’t have to bring a portable gas stove, did you! And what’s in that cooler… isn’t that the fondue I’d frozen?
“With this, there’s no doubt we’ll be getting delicious meals until our lives stabilize!”
“You’re really well-prepared.”
“Why on earth did you bring stuff like this…?”
“Huh? I didn’t want to go without eating your cooking over there, and since it takes time to make, this is just to tide us over until then.”
Oh, I see… You… Is it really a good idea to have brought that here on purpose? Should I say the timing is just too perfect?
“So, big bro. Go cook this up.”
“Why do I have to be ordered around to cook in a place like this, even after coming to another world?”
“Just cook it. It’s your job, right?”
“I’ll punch you, you little brat!”
“Hahahaha! Raphtalia, while big bro is cooking, let’s gather some intel. That’s our job, OK? Big bro.”

……I guess it’s better than just standing around watching? It’s better than me going out on my own. Do my little brother and Raphtalia even know how to fight? I’m sure they’re fine with weapons, but I wonder if they can handle the rest.
“Sigh… Fine, I guess.”
“Make a bunch of different things, okay!”
“Yeah, yeah.”
“Well then… um, I’m worried, so I’m going with you. Naofumi-san.”
“Ah, just keep an eye on him so he doesn’t go on some reckless rampage.”

I’d be in trouble if that “Yahoo from another world” got carried away and ended up getting hurt or killed. So, I watched as my younger brother and Raphtalia headed toward the village to gather information. Hmm… they’ve brought back quite a lot. Flour, vegetables, potatoes, eggs, and seasonings. That’s pretty much all the food. That’s his stuff. To be honest, I’d like to save some and make it last a while… but he keeps telling me to make all sorts of things, so if I don’t prepare at least three different dishes, he’ll probably get on my nerves. Oh well. We’ve got water, so I’m sure we’ll manage. …With these ingredients, I can make the Hero’s favorite dishes. I guess that’ll do. And so, with a sigh, I began cooking.
†(ᐢ⓿ᴥ⓿ᐢ）

I never imagined I’d end up transported to a world different from my own. I mean, I understand that we, as God Hunters, have already set out on our journey and are in the midst of battle, but for us to have come to Japan… well. And not only that, but Lord Naofumi’s younger brother—and even the people who were originally riding in the front car of the train… Whether it was coincidence or fate—or if it was a deliberate attempt to target Lord Naofumi—is hard to say. With these suspicions in mind, we’re currently talking to the villagers. For now, we’ve learned that it’ll take a while for the lord to arrive, and that it’s better to have some way to defend ourselves. Also, his younger brother was casually chatting with them to find out if there was anything we could do to help, since we’ll be relying on their hospitality. According to Lord Naofumi, he’s someone who cares about appearances… but he’s actually quite shrewd. Enough that you could believe he and Lord Naofumi are brothers. Also, since I’ve sparred with him quite a bit, I know his swordsmanship is quite skilled. He’s not quite on the level of the Sword Hero, but if he gains experience in actual combat, he has a high chance of improving.
“But another world, huh… My brother is actually a valuable asset, so I hope this incident helps him gain some confidence—or at least a better understanding?”

According to Naofumi-sama, she thinks he’s making fun of him, but she does say things to me that could certainly be taken that way. She’ll occasionally give me a flirtatious look and ask, “Why don’t you switch to me?”—though I turn her down every time. She even parried a thrust aimed at Fohl-kun with her elbow.
“Naofumi-san is good at defensive combat, you know.”
“Haha, it seems even Raphtalia-san doesn’t understand my brother’s combat prowess.”

No, I understand it all too well—it actually hurts! Naofumi-sama’s fighting style is specialized in defense, you know? I think Atla is about the only other person besides me who really gets it. As I watched, his younger brother made a slight motion to brush back his bangs and shot me a sharp—or rather, piercing—glance.
“Haven’t you seen it either, Raphtalia? The aerial move my brother does while cooking.”
When he said that, I looked away but nodded.
“Yes, it’s an amazing move, isn’t it?”

I’ve always wondered if it could be applied to swordplay. Even the Sword Hero’s eyes widened when he saw Naofumi-sama doing it in that other world. To begin with… when facing Takt, it seems Naofumi-sama is skilled enough with a sword to almost perfectly replicate Eclair-san’s techniques just by watching her.
“That’s why I think he could fight in an emergency.”
“But I think we should be the ones to fight, don’t you?”
“Hmm… This is exactly why Raphtalia and the others are such a pain. If they were the type to let their big brother do the fighting while they stayed safe, I’d chase them away without hesitation.”
…Does this mean your younger brother is subtly driving away people who try to take advantage of Lord Naofumi?
“Hey, big brother. Have you ever heard him say why he doesn’t do kendo or something, even though he can pull off such amazing techniques…?”
“No… He did say he wasn’t really interested, though. And he also mentioned that his athletic ability isn’t all that great.”
In the world I came from, it wasn’t really suited to his stats, so he never learned it—but I suppose this is for a different reason.
“I guess he won’t say, huh? Well… it wouldn’t be strange if he did, but Big Brother has had a lot of experiences like that, you know.”
His younger brother muttered, sounding somewhat resigned.
“So… Naofumi, what happened to you? ”
What could be so bad that he wouldn’t even learn swordsmanship?

“Sigh. Well, since it’s you, Raphtalia, I guess I’ll tell you. The reason my older brother doesn’t do kendo even though I do is—he usually says it’s just that he isn’t interested—but he does try out trial lessons or go for a few lessons here and there.”

It’s true that Lord Naofumi seems to be involved in all sorts of things in this world. He gets invited to part-time jobs a lot, and sometimes I don’t even know what kind of work he’s doing on any given day. In the same way, I suppose he gives things a try when he gets interested. Though he does say he isn’t as versatile as the Spear Hero.
“So, getting back to kendo… Well, when I told my parents I was interested and wanted to try it, my older brother ended up joining too.”
“Right.”
How does that connect to that aerial move? I have absolutely no idea.

“So, I went to a dojo in the neighborhood to take lessons, and the assistant instructor there said to me, ‘I’ve never seen anyone this untalented,’ he said. Well, I got absolutely trashed. I was trying to keep up with my older brother, so maybe I was a little cocky. ‘You’re telling me I have no talent?’ I said something stupid without thinking of the consequences.”

Yes, as if confessing his own sins, the younger brother looked a bit pained… he spoke with the same embarrassed look as the Spear Hero and the other heroes. Does Lord Naofumi often make those around him feel guilty?

“You know that older brother of mine? I figured, ‘Well, if he’s got no talent, there’s nothing to be done about it,’ so I quit pretty quickly. My family just accepted it and let me quit. Plus, with the age difference, I was competing with him, so I felt like I’d beaten my older brother.”

It seems there was a slight difference in how Lord Naofumi and his younger brother were viewed within the family. However… from what I’ve seen, the younger brother was an excellent student, while Naofumi-sama was versatile and dependable—it seemed more like a difference in their paths rather than him being particularly disadvantaged.

“I used to look down on him back then, though… While I was cleaning up the dojo after practicing kendo for a while, I happened to overhear something. The assistant instructor was having a conversation I couldn’t ignore with a student he favored.”
From his younger brother’s perspective, it was a slightly menacing expression—one that could be interpreted as either a tale of valor or a story of revenge.

“‘That’s Iwatani’s older brother. If he’d kept at it, he might have surpassed me, so I made him quit. He’s got no guts, does he? Well, if he’d kept going, I would’ve crushed him,’ he said, bragging as if it were a point of pride.”
“…He sounds like a petty person.”
It seems the assistant instructor who tried to teach Naofumi-sama had some serious character flaws.
“So what about me? I wasn’t told I had no talent. Well, that really made me angry.”
“You’re still practicing kendo, right?”

“Yeah, at a different dojo. The assistant instructor there… Hehe, he suffered a career-ending injury during practice and had no choice but to quit. Man, that guy wasn’t even strong—no one could improve under him. He was really weak.”

As he said this, my younger brother wore an eerie smile. I wonder if, somehow, even as a child, he made sure that person got what was coming to him? This younger brother seems like the kind who’d be scared of the Spear Hero. I thought this earlier too, but it’s true… he’s actually pretty strong. Looks like he has a trophy in his room. I guess he won some tournament or something.

“So, I told my older brother that assistant instructor had issues, but he wouldn’t believe me. By that time, he was already going, ‘Look, look!’ and doing that aerial move… you know? It was such a letdown. Haaaaaah.”
That’s a very deep sigh.
“Well… it’s a rare kind of relationship where he makes warm meals and waits for us, filling in for our parents who are usually away working. He even makes us bento boxes.”
He’s talking about Naofumi-sama with such a gentle look in his eyes. It seems he really cares about him.
“Anyway, I think he’d develop pretty well if he gave it a try, but he just won’t do swordsmanship—though he’d be fine with something else, too.”
“Y-yeah, you’re right.”
It’s true—for someone who’s supposedly clumsy, he’s got excellent eyesight and can spot openings… and above all, he’s been training with that Atla-san, hasn’t he?
“You really care about Naofumi, don’t you?”
I’d suspected as much. Even though he often talks down to people or acts strangely selfish, he also seems to be acting a bit spoiled.

“Well, I guess a big part of it is just that it’s annoying how unfairly underrated I am. He brags about how he ‘reformed me’ through video games, right? Since Mom and Dad’s opinion of me was way too low, I just put on a little show for them—and he’s been turning that into a heroic tale ever since.”
“I wonder when he’ll finally realize?” his younger brother said, wearing a mocking expression that looked just like Naofumi-sama’s. …This guy is actually pretty sharp, you know?
“It’s not a lie that I was curious about the games my older brother used to play, though. Thanks to that, my cram school and extracurriculars got a lot lighter, so I actually had time to play.”
He’s quite the character. As expected… he’s a troublesome guy who isn’t exactly straightforward.
“So. Did you notice, Raphtalia-san?”
“Notice what?”
“This village, you see—”
“Waaaaaah!?”
“Gyaaaaaaaah!?”
Just as his younger brother was about to say that, screams rang out, along with a commotion coming from the area where the person who had been boasting about serving food to everyone was standing.
“Something seems to have happened. Let’s go!”
Acting on instinct, I dashed toward the screams.
“Yeah. Looks like some kind of commotion’s breaking out.”

Saying that, my younger brother picked up a handy wooden stick and followed right behind me. When we reached the scene, there was… a monster that looked like a fried shrimp, jumping around and lunging at people. You could say it looked like a flea, too.
“Gyaaa!? H-help me!”
As it lunged at me, I quickly unfurled my hammer and smashed it.
“Splash, splash!?”
“Eeeeeek!?”
“Whaaaat! What on earth is this monster?”
When I squinted, its name appeared on the screen.
Ebifura
It’s exactly what it sounds like. It’s the kind of name Naofumi-sama would come up with. Well, actually, there are names with a similar sense of humor in my world, too.
“Whoa, it kind of looks like a fried shrimp.”
My younger brother also hit Ebifura with a wooden stick to make it bounce away.
“H-Help meeeeeee!”

And the one screaming the loudest—the one the monsters were swarming toward—was the student who’d been bragging about his cooking. I stepped in front of him to protect him and took a defensive stance.
“You people from another world! You’ve done something outrageous!”
“What on earth did these people do!?”
The villagers rushed over, clutching anything they could use as a weapon.
“I didn’t do anything!　I was just cooking for everyone using the utensils and ingredients I had on hand! But then the finished dish suddenly swelled up—”
“That’s it! You! You carelessly cooked and created a Cooking Monster! Don’t cook when you can’t even fight!”
“A Cooking Monster? What do you mean?”

“In this world, when you perform actions called ‘cooking’—like heating or cutting food—the ingredients react and turn into monsters. These monsters are the condensed resentment of the monsters that became ingredients, and they attack not only the cook who prepared the dish but also the people eating it. If you absolutely must cook, you have to be approved by the dish itself!”
“Ah, so that’s why there are no kitchens in people’s homes—I figured everyone must gather somewhere to cook.”

……What kind of world setting—or rather, logic—is that? My younger brother said this as if he’d already noticed. This is what he was about to say earlier, isn’t it? In my case… since there was a dining hall in the village, most ordinary homes didn’t have kitchens. Anyway, I’ve learned that there are all kinds of worlds as a God Hunter, but I never imagined a world like this actually existed.
“That’s why you mustn’t cook lightly. Eating something delicious becomes a life-or-death battle. The tastier it is, the stronger the Cooking Monster becomes. You mustn’t make delicious food!”
“Then what about that dried meat and bread?” I thought to myself, but I asked aloud.
“What kind of world is this… you say!? Lord Naofumi!?”
“Big Brother!?”

Lord Naofumi’s cooking is incredibly delicious. And right now, Lord Naofumi himself is cooking!? Just as the thought of Lord Naofumi crossed our minds, a black shadow suddenly appeared on the scene and swiftly took down the Ebi-Flers one by one.
“‘Splash-splash—!?’”
After taking a powerful blow, the Ebifura stopped moving… no, with a “plop,” they turned into fried shrimp and lined up on a plate.
“Shuu!”
“Gette!”
“Dessh!”

The shadows came to a sudden halt and watched us. Um… first up is a bird-like monster with a stew-like pattern on its belly, holding something more like a shovel than a spoon. Next is a pig-like monster holding a fork, with thick, red, noodle-like hair. And finally, a rabbit-like monster with a cream-colored body coated in a candy-like glaze and reddish-purple ears, wielding a large skewer. Their names were Fenichu, Napogetti, and University Rabbit.
“This is… what an incredible amount of cooking energy!?”
“They’re Cooking Monsters with incredible power! Hey! What should we do?”
“This is bad. Even an A-class chef might not be able to defeat them!”

The villagers held their breath as they faced off against the monsters. What should we do? I’d like to go to Lord Naofumi first, but the situation doesn’t allow for that right now. What is “Cooking Energy”? Well, I do feel like I’m sensing some kind of incredible power… Is that it?
“Oh, you guys are here too?”
Just then, Lord Naofumi arrived.
“Shuu!”
“Get!”
“Dish!”
The monsters charged straight toward Lord Naofumi.
“Big brother, get out of the way!”
“Lord Naofumi!”
We stepped forward to block their path, but Lord Naofumi stepped in front of us first. However, he didn’t even raise his shield or take a defensive stance…
“Shuu!”
“Gette!”
“Dessh!”
The monsters stopped right next to Lord Naofumi and bowed their heads as if in submission.
“Ah… well, I guess you’ve quelled the commotion? Good job.”
“Shuu!!”
“Gette!!”
“Dessh!!”
“What gracious words!” The monsters displayed such obvious joy that even I could tell.
“What on earth is this?”

“Ah, I thought I’d just finished cooking, but then all the food turned into this form, bowed their heads, and started fawning over me? When I heard screams, I told them to go quieten things down, and they dashed off.”
“I wonder why?” Naofumi-sama tilted his head in puzzlement, just as the villagers gasped and began clasping their hands in prayer.
“To subdue Cooking Monsters without making a contract that imposes the constraint of fighting to earn their recognition and elevate the dish to a higher level…”
“Is it because the Cooking Monsters are satisfied!?”
“What do you think, you guys?”
“Shu!!”
“Gette!!”
“Dessh!!”
In response to the villagers’ question, the three Cooking Monsters nodded.
“How amazing… to be accepted as the ultimate dish, one powerful enough to purify their own regrets… I’d love to have just one bite.”
With their hands clasped in prayer, the villagers pleaded with Lord Naofumi.
“Are you the god of cooking?”
“To hell with gods!”
Lord Naofumi instinctively recoiled in disgust at the word “god.” Given his past experiences, he couldn’t help but react that way.
“My fried shrimp… they just wouldn’t do what I told them to.”

The guy who was cooking so arrogantly is being ignored. Well, actually, they are talking about eating the fried shrimp together. But since the villagers are saying Lord Naofumi’s cooking is even more amazing, everyone’s attention is focused on him.
“So you’re a chef!”
“No, I’m a college student, but…”
“You’ll be an amazing chef someday.”
“Shut up!”
Naofumi-sama just scolded his younger brother. I do think he’s bound to be a successful chef in the future, though.
“Anyway, big bro. About these monsters…”
“Ah, you mean the dishes I made for you and Raphtalia?”
“Oh, right! So how are we supposed to eat them?”
“You, man…”

Um, if we think of it in terms of the monsters we’ve defeated, does that mean they’ll come back to life if we defeat them? After all, Lord Naofumi is very lenient and kind to monsters who look up to him. Like the Raph-species, the Tari species, and even Raph-chan!
“Shu”
“Gette”
“Dessh”
And when the monsters held out their hands toward Lord Naofumi, cards suddenly appeared.
“What’s this?”

“Those are recipe cards. As long as you have these cards, even if you turn the dish back into a monster and eat it, you can summon the same creature by recreating the exact same dish. You can also store them without eating them. As long as you don’t turn them into a dish, they won’t rot. However, if you lose a battle, you’ll have to cook the dish again. Even if you make the same dish, only one monster will appear.”
That said, he explained that if you consciously try to create new ones individually, you can increase their number.
“Huh… It’s kind of like those capsule monsters from somewhere. You guys—if I give the order, will you listen to someone else?”
The monsters nodded in response to Naofumi-sama’s question. Then the monsters returned to their cards.
“Hmm… What a strange world.”
That’s for sure.

“Oh… God of Cooking, please protect us from the bandit chefs who repeatedly raid our village with their Cooking Monsters. If you do, the local nobles will surely treat us people from another world with respect.”
“What kind of logic is that…?”
“We agree with you on that point, too.”
“Hahaha! Big bro, that’s quite the compliment. That’s great, isn’t it?”
His younger brother is laughing. He seems to be in a good mood.
“Well, whatever. So then…”
Lord Naofumi cleared his throat lightly.
“This is the world of the Cooking Monsters—let’s shorten it to… Kukimon?”
“What are you imitating?!”
Lord Naofumi is definitely just messing around.
“It’s a parody of ‘Capsule Monster’!”
“I guess so.”
“‘Kukimon’ is fine, but ‘Gurumon’ or ‘Tabemon’ would work too.”
I wish his younger brother would play along too!
“You and Raphtalia—each of you pick one from this group. Let’s start with Raphtalia.”

Huh? Are we taking them with us? Wouldn’t it be better to just fight them normally? With a flick of his wrist, Naofumi summoned the Cooking Monsters. It’s Fenichu, Napogetti, and Daigaku Usagi, right?
“From left to right: Ren, Itsuki, and Motoyasu. Pick one of them and go teach those bandit chefs a lesson.”
“Shu!”
“Gette!”
“Dessh!”
“Let’s do this!”—it’s great that they’re so energetic, but… what on earth is this?! Plus, judging by the villagers’ reactions, they seem to be pretty strong.
“These kids have official species names, you know. I mean, even if they’re those people’s favorite foods, isn’t it a bit much to name the Cooking Monsters after them?”
“Big bro. Ren’s based on stew, right? Why didn’t you name one after me?”
“It’d get confusing if you were standing right here.”
These brothers… I just don’t get what they’re so particular about.
“Anyway, I’m in the mood to make something else. I’m thinking of making chicken rice or a kids’ meal, so go gather the ingredients.”
“What are you planning to make?!”
“Well, I’ll shape it before it’s done and make it look like… oops.”
“You’re planning to make something that looks like Raph-chan! I don’t want that!”
“Raph-chan? Is that Raphtalia-san’s pet or something?”
And so, our… battle in this strange world began.
April Fools' Day
